examples.question_text:
Write these amounts in decimal litres.
(a) $3$ L $47$ mL
(b) $86$ mL
examples.solution_text:
(a) $47\text{ mL}=0.047\text{ L}$.
$3\text{ L }47\text{ mL}=3.047\text{ L}$.
(b) $86\text{ mL}$ is $86$ thousandths of a litre.
$86\text{ mL}=0.086\text{ L}$.

examples.question_text:
Interpret these amounts.
(a) $6.208$ L as litres and millilitres
(b) $0.019$ L as millilitres
examples.solution_text:
(a) $6.208\text{ L}=6\text{ L}+0.208\text{ L}$.
$0.208\text{ L}=208\text{ mL}$.
The amount is $6\text{ L }208\text{ mL}$.
(b) $0.019\times1000=19$.
$0.019\text{ L}=19\text{ mL}$.

examples.question_text:
(a) A jug contains $1.8$ L of water. Another $73$ mL is added. Write the new amount in litres to three decimal places.
(b) Which amount is greater: $1.804$ L or $1$ L $84$ mL?
(c) Complete the digit: $5.0\square6$ L $=5086$ mL.
examples.solution_text:
(a) $73\text{ mL}=0.073\text{ L}$.
$1.800+0.073=1.873$.
The new amount is $1.873\text{ L}$.
(b) $1\text{ L }84\text{ mL}=1.084\text{ L}$.
$1.804>1.084$, so $1.804\text{ L}$ is greater.
(c) $5086\text{ mL}=5.086\text{ L}$.
The missing digit is $8$.

examples.question_text:
Convert these capacities.
(a) $2470$ mL to litres
(b) $0.0524$ L to millilitres
examples.solution_text:
(a) Divide by $1000$ to change millilitres to litres.
$2470\div1000=2.470$.
$2470\text{ mL}=2.47\text{ L}$.

(b) Multiply by $1000$ to change litres to millilitres.
$0.0524\times1000=52.4$.
$0.0524\text{ L}=52.4\text{ mL}$.
